judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard preamble, but it recites 'by and among' for only two parties and identifies Clearwire Spectrum Holdings II LLC as a Nevada LLC; nothing here has two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble names only Licensee and Clearwire as 'Parties', yet Article V has Licensee representing to 'Clearwire and Clearwire Parent', Article VI has Clearwire Parent making representations, and Section 4.02(c)(iii)(2) speaks of 'each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto' — a genuine incoherence about who is bound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals introduce loaded characterizations ('Total Consideration', 'would not have been executed but for all of the elements') whose legal effect is contestable, though the language itself is not internally ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital language that the IUAs 'would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration' and that Licensee is a 'shareholder of Clearwire Corporation' cuts against the operative refund and termination machinery in Sections 2.02 and 9.01, a classic recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive overview defining 'EBS Spectrum Capacity' with the odd qualifier 'collectively, when under IUA hereunder'; that qualifier is loose but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with Sections 1.02 and 4.02, though the 'when under IUA' limitation could matter against Section 7.06's reference to 'Licensee's EBS Spectrum'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Characterizing the initial payment as exceeding 'the value of the Initial Spectrum Capacity' while being consideration for the Option and ROFR and also an 'advance payment' invites competing readings of what the $23M actually bought.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 2.01 (Prepaid Royalties applied against IUA amounts) and Section 2.02 (full refund of the unapplied balance), the statement that part of the payment is consideration for the Option and ROFR is hard to reconcile with a right to refund the entire unapplied balance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'which consists of, among other items (i)...(iv), together with technology, facilities, equipment and other functionality' is an open-ended list against enumerated specifics — the reach of the catch-all is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-references ARTICLE II and ARTICLE III (miskeyed as 'ARTICLE I]' and 'ARTICLE II'), and the enumerated benefits track Sections 3.03, 3.04, 3.08 and 3.09 without evident conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR-mangled defined-term references ('TUA', 'ARTICLE II') aside, the exchange it describes is definite and the defined term 'Access Right Royalties' is anchored to ARTICLE III.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.01(c) and the recitals treat Access Right Royalties as a separate limb of the Total Consideration, consistent with this provision; no operative conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Option is an agreement to negotiate price 'in good faith based on fair market value' subject to a $0.15/MHz POP cap, and turns on the undefined-in-text trigger 'Available' — both are prime candidates for competing constructions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Section 1.04 (ROFR), Section 1.02(d) (lapse on Term expiry), Section 2.02 (Term not deemed expired while Option periods run) and Section 9.03 (survival), and those provisions pull in different directions on when the Option dies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains outright mechanical errors ('a GSA the covers the same metropolitan are in Puerto Rico') and a defined 'Substantially Similar' that is circular, plus a $0.15 ceiling sitting against a $0.10 floor in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its price mechanics (Higher Price / MFN) can exceed the $0.15 per MHz POP cap fixed in Section 1.02(b), and its twelve-month post-Term survival is in tension with Section 9.01's Term and Section 1.02(d)'s lapse rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and mostly definite, but 'Available' is a boundary term and the carve-out for prior notice of 'intention to exercise' is loosely drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic lapse of Options on Term expiry conflicts with Section 9.03 (Options survive termination if the triggering event occurred earlier) and with Section 2.02's proviso that the Term is not deemed expired while Option periods remain open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Obligates Clearwire to 'cause' unnamed Service Affiliates to assume liability, with the scope of 'such additional agreements as may be required' left vague; still, the last sentence preserves Clearwire's primary obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the ARTICLE III Access Right Royalties and the 'Collateral Document' concept used in Section 1.01(a); no contradictory provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but mostly mechanical; the fair-market-value substitution and 'other terms that are more favorable to the third party' comparison are judgment-laden but procedurally channelled to arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its carve-out depends on compliance with the Section 1.02(b) Option Notice and it expressly survives a failed Option negotiation, while Section 1.02(d) and Section 9.03 give inconsistent signals on post-Term survival of ROFR rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The $23,000,000 figure and payment trigger are definite; the only softness is 'applied as provided in Section 1.02(b)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.02(b) addresses application only to Future Spectrum Capacity IUAs while this section says the Prepaid Royalties apply to Initial and Future IUAs, and Section 4.01(b)(iii) separately requires delivery of an 'Upfront Royalty' under each IUA — the relationship among these payments is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso that 'the Term shall not be deemed to have expired for this purpose during a period that the Option periods described in Section 1.02(b) have not terminated' is opaque, and Clearwire's unilateral power to extend the refund date and thereby extend the Term is an unusual, contestable mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.01 defines the Term as ending when Licensee returns the entire unused Prepaid Royalties, so the refund duty triggered by expiration of the Term and the Term ending on refund are circular; this is the sharpest whole-instrument incoherence in the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commercially reasonable best efforts to enter into a joint venture', 'consider in good faith', and the odd trailing condition about pricing 'greater than Clearwire's lowest wholesale price' are vague and grammatically awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The benchmark to third-party agreements sits alongside Section 3.05's 'lowest wholesale rate' standard without contradiction, though the Puerto Rico carve-out echoes Section 1.02(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence pointer to Sections 3.02–3.04; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 3.03 and 3.04 and with Section 1.01(c)'s listing of the Access Right Royalties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the same capacity and characteristics as the highest level of premium mass market retail service' and 'individuals that are associated with an Educational End User at the time' are elastic standards that could be read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subjecting the accounts to Clearwire's 'then generally applicable Acceptable Use Policy' subject to non-inconsistency with the Agreement leaves a workable hierarchy; Section 3.05(a) expressly incorporates this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in such locations served by the Clearwire National Platform on a full time basis as Licensee desires' is loosely bounded, and the 5% Educational Reservation is tied to shifting FCC Rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers disputes to the 'Dispute Resolution Procedure', which Section 10.11 defines (in truncated form) as the sole means of resolution — a workable fit, and Section 3.04 expressly builds on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'adjusted upward every five years proportionate to the growth of the overall data capacity' measured by 'average throughput' in a manner 'as shall be agreed' is an agreement to agree with a vague metric.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It calls the accounts 'Basic Cost-Free Education Account' while Sections 1.01(c) and 3.04 call the same thing 'Educational Reservation Basic Cost-Free Educational Accounts', and the five-year adjustment sits beside Section 3.04(a)'s annual recalculation without a stated ordering.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short 'in addition to and not in lieu of' introduction with the computation deferred to the subsections; nothing ambiguous stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates cleanly with Sections 3.02(a) and 3.03 on stacking of accounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on undefined-in-text units 'Sector' and 'Market Area' and on the greater-of comparison; the annual recalculation date is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Formula Quantity subsection and Section 3.05's cap of twice the Cost-Free Accounts; the five-year adjustment in Section 3.03(b) is on a different cycle but applies to a different account type.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection is mislabelled '(3)' where '(i)' is plainly intended, and 'rounded up or down to the nearest whole number' is redundant but harmless; the Local Channel Ratio itself is defined with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(b) cross-refers to 'Sections 3.04(a)(ii)', which depends on this mis-numbering being read as intended, but nothing substantive conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'officially associated with' an Educational End User and the resale prohibition are illustrated by an example, which helps, though the boundary of 'Educational End User environment' remains soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(b) expressly excepts this section and Section 3.05 from the no-resale covenant, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A timing rule keyed to commercial launch or the Commencement Date, whichever is later; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.01's 'from and after the Commencement Date of an IUA'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'lowest wholesale rate provided by Clearwire to an arms-length third party in such Market Area or other comparable market' leaves the comparator set genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.01's Puerto Rico joint-venture proviso uses a slightly different benchmark ('Clearwire's lowest wholesale price in the market'), a mild mismatch rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to 'any Licensee requesting' when there is a single Licensee, and 'thirty (30) days after the availability of such services' is a loose trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to a 'standard Clearwire wholesale agreement form ... consistent with the terms of this Agreement and the applicable IUA', which is subordinated rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '10% above Clearwire's cost to acquire' is a definite formula, though 'cost' is unelaborated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale restriction matches Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.08(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'generally provided', 'reasonably necessary support', and 'as contemplated by their agreement' (whose agreement?) are all soft, and the six-month lag is oddly phrased as an outer limit rather than an entitlement date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(c) lets Clearwire restrict capabilities for capacity reasons, which cuts against the unqualified 'full use' language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the same degree of access ... that is provided to premium third party content providers' turns on an undefined comparator class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by Section 3.08(c)'s capacity carve-out, which is expressly cross-referenced, so the fit is intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'most favored program suppliers' and 'educational in nature' are undefined evaluative terms, and the cross-reference is garbled ('Sections 3.04(a)(i1)').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale covenant expressly excepts Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.05, harmonising with the MVNO right; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'no longer commercially and technically feasible due to limitations in network capabilities' is a vague, unilaterally-invoked standard reserved to the drafter's benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs Clearwire to 'comply with the provisions of ARTICLE III to ensure timely access to information about capacity usage', but ARTICLE III contains no such information-access provisions — a broken internal reference, and the restriction right cuts against Sections 3.07 and 3.08(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commercially reasonable best efforts' is an internally mixed standard and 'one ordinary unpaid channel carried on such entity's basic tier' is imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limited Reciprocity is listed in Section 1.01(c) as a core Access Right Royalty, yet here it is only a best-efforts undertaking at Licensee's cost — a tension between the described bundle and the operative promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the following actions required of it by subsections (a) through (c)' uses a singular pronoun for two parties, a trivial slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsections (a)-(c) exist and match; nothing elsewhere contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing-deliverables list; definite items, though the Wire Account language ('each a Wire Account') suggests plural accounts where one is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'Schedule 4.01', which does not appear in the Agreement's List of Schedules (only Schedule A and the Licensee Schedule), and to Exhibit III, which the exhibit list confirms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deliverables are enumerated and definite on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (iii) requires delivery of 'the Upfront Royalty provided for in the applicable EBS Spectrum Capacity IUA', a payment concept nowhere reconciled with the $23,000,000 Prepaid Royalties in Section 2.01 or the refund mechanics of Section 2.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Routine officers' certificate requirement; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'each other Party' in a two-party agreement, a harmless residue, and matches Sections 4.01(a)(iii) and 4.01(b)(ii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Initial Closing and Initial Closing Date by reference to the Effective Date; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble's Effective Date and Section 4.01's execution deliveries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall take place as specified in the applicable IUAs when the Parties reach agreement on the pricing' makes the closing contingent on an agreement that may never be reached.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Section 1.02(b) negotiation process, which expressly permits Clearwire to walk away, so the two fit — though the Subsequent Closing Date/Effective Date equation must be squared with Section 10.02's survival period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'No Injunctions or Restraints' condition is a sentence fragment with no operative verb ('No temporary restraining order ... preventing the consummation'), so what must be true at closing is stated only by implication.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to a single 'following condition' and then lists one; nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard closing conditions with a clear waiver mechanic; the reference to representations 'contained in the IUA' rather than in this Agreement is deliberate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Licensee subsection is also numbered '(ii)', a numbering collision, but the substance dovetails with Section 4.01(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror-image conditions, clearly drafted apart from the mis-numbering carried over from the preceding subsection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires resolutions of 'each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto', but the Preamble names no Clearwire Affiliate as a Party — an unreconciled reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The general rule (electronic delivery) and the proviso (Initial Closing at named offices) are stated in one breath and sit uneasily together, though the proviso plainly governs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement fixes a closing location; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable best efforts' and 'necessary, proper or advisable' are conventional further-assurances language whose reach is broad but rarely determinative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.07's 'commercially reasonable best efforts' standard is a different formulation of a similar duty, but the two are not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organization and good-standing representation with a Material Adverse Effect qualifier; definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The lead-in runs the representation to 'Clearwire and Clearwire Parent', although Clearwire Parent is not made a Party by the Preamble — a recurring who-is-bound problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate authorization and enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy and equity carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'on the date hereof' limitation differs from Clearwire's mirror in Section 6.02, which is not so limited, but that asymmetry is deliberate rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation with enumerated categories and a materiality exception; nothing genuinely elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by Schedule 5.03, which is not in the document's List of Schedules, but that is a disclosure-schedule gap rather than an internal conflict.
